name: Audit 8 remaining future-dated deadline literals in integration fixtures for the PR #2803 date-bomb class (earliest detonates 2026-12-31)
description: Surfaced by WI-2993's sibling sweep over the PR #2803 repair (a literal 2026-08-01 UTC grace deadline in payment-failed-alert.integration.test.ts that expired and reddened the required `main` job on every API PR until repaired 2026-08-01). The class is PROVEN live in this repo, so the question is only whether siblings exist. SWEEP METHOD (reproduce with: git grep -nE "(deadline|expire|expiresAt|periodEnd|cycleReset|grace|validUntil|renewsAt|trialEnd|until)[A-Za-z]*:?\\s*[:=]?\\s*.*'20(26-(09|1[0-2])|2[7-9]|3[0-9])" -- '*.test.ts' '*.test.tsx' '*fixtures*'): 11 deadline-shaped future literals found on origin/main at 2026-08-08. A literal is only a BOMB when the code under test compares it against the REAL clock; where the test injects an explicit `now`, the future-vs-deadline relationship is fixed forever and the literal is inert. CLEARED AS SAFE (clock injected, verified by reading the call site): billing/trial.integration.test.ts:211 (cycleStillFuture 2027-01-01, but resetDailyQuotas is passed NOW = 2026-05-15); scripts/reconcile-worker-secrets.test.ts:75 (validUntil 2026-10-28, but validateOwnershipManifest is passed new Date('2026-08-01')); the mentor-notice/now-feed/session-exchange 2026-09-06 literals, which ARE the injected `now` rather than a deadline. NOT CLEARED — 8 literals seeded into the DB and consumed by production code whose clock source was NOT traced (this is the remaining work, and the reason this item exists): identity-v2/country-policy-loader.integration.test.ts:126,180 legalReviewValidUntil 2026-12-31 (EARLIEST — a legal-review validity window is exactly the shape that would be compared to real now and reject an expired policy); identity-v2/family-join-journey.integration.test.ts:202 legalReviewValidUntil 2027-08-01; tests/integration/billing-service.integration.test.ts:456,709,716 top-up credit expiresAt 2027-01-01/2027-02-01 (credit consumption commonly filters expiresAt > now()); billing/billing-v2/family-v2.integration.test.ts:353,415,612,657 periodEndAt/expiresAt 2027-01-01/2027-01-31/2027-06-15 — SAME billing family as the literal that actually detonated; billing/metering.integration.test.ts:162 and middleware/metering.integration.test.ts:134 expiresAt 2027-04-01/2027-06-01; identity-v2/export-v2.integration.test.ts:546 expiresAt 2027-01-01. NOTE the repair pattern to copy where a bomb is confirmed: PR #2803 replaced the literal with a run-clock-relative constant (new Date(Date.now() + 30 days)), which cannot re-expire on any future run date; a frozen injected clock is the equally valid alternative and is what the cleared cases already use.
acceptanceCriteria: For each of the 8 uncleared literals: trace the production code path that consumes the seeded field and record whether it compares against the real clock or an injected one. Each literal ends in exactly one of two states, stated explicitly with the call site cited: (a) INERT - the consuming path takes an injected clock, so the relationship is fixed and no change is made; or (b) BOMB - the consuming path uses the real clock, in which case the literal is replaced with a run-clock-relative value (the PR #2803 pattern) or the test is given an explicit injected now, and the detonation date it would have had is recorded. Done: no future-dated deadline literal in an integration fixture is in an unknown state, and the earliest surviving detonation date across the repo is either eliminated or knowingly accepted with a date and an owner.
